activity.role: Lord Protector of England for Edward V before becoming king
activity.notes: Richard (Duke of Gloucester) served as Lord Protector for his young nephew Edward V in 1483 before becoming King Richard III in June. This earlier protectorship was a distinct government office, not the same reign as his 1483–1485 kingship. Exact month/day not asserted until independent official evidence confirms.

sources.title: The Royal Family — Edward V (Protector Richard, Duke of Gloucester)
sources.citation_text: The Royal Family's Edward V biography states that Edward V was a minor and that Richard, Duke of Gloucester, was made Protector by Edward IV's will, before Richard took the throne in mid-June 1483. This source supports the earlier Lord Protector office rather than using Richard III's kingly biography as a substitute.

sources.title: The National Archives — Richard III: From Protector to King, 1483
sources.citation_text: UK National Archives records Richard, Duke of Gloucester, exercising the protectorship under Edward V in spring/June 1483, before becoming King Richard III. Its archival exhibition includes Edward V and Gloucester's signatures on a June 1483 warrant and contemporary material. Protector and King are distinct offices; no exact appointment day is inferred here.
